subject.title: Feature: Subscribe to WhatsApp call events (Baileys)

question: Should inbound WhatsApp call activity be exposed only as transient opt-in events, or should OpenClaw retain durable per-contact call history for later agent queries?
rationale: The two designs have materially different privacy, identity-resolution, storage, migration, configuration, and public API contracts, which automation should not choose.

options.title: Transient event surface
options.body: Expose sanitized opt-in call events through a documented WhatsApp-owned hook or session-event contract without retaining historical activity.

options.title: Durable contact history
options.body: Store normalized call activity in the per-agent SQLite database and define identity, retention, migration, and query semantics before implementation.

options.title: Decline inbound tracking
options.body: Keep the existing message-only inbound model and leave relationship-history tracking to an external integration.

recommendation.title: Transient event surface
recommendation.body: Expose sanitized opt-in call events through a documented WhatsApp-owned hook or session-event contract without retaining historical activity.

likelyOwner.reason: The current history and issue discussion connect this person most directly to WhatsApp channel architecture, call capability, and the required privacy boundary.
